24 A car is travelling at a constant velocity directly towards a man standing in the middle of the road.
The driver sounds the car’s horn as a warning. The horn emits a sound wave of constant
frequency.
The frequency of the sound heard by the man is different from the frequency of the sound emitted
by the horn.
Which statement is correct?
A
The frequency of the sound emitted by the horn is greater than the frequency of the sound
heard by the man.
B
The frequency of the sound heard by the man depends on the distance between the car and
the man.
C
The sound waves continually accelerate as they move from the horn to the man.
D
The wavelength of the sound heard by the man is less than the wavelength of the sound
emitted by the horn.

hints: Notice the car is the moving source travelling directly towards the stationary man while the horn frequency stays constant.
Recall that sound speed in air stays constant, so the moving source catches up with the wavefronts it has just emitted in the forward direction.
Use $v = f \lambda$ at the stationary observer to link the crowded wavefront spacing to the frequency he hears.
walkthrough: Identify the situation: moving source approaching a stationary observer, with source frequency $f_s$ constant and car velocity constant towards the man.
State the governing physics: wave speed $v$ in air is fixed by the medium, so motion of the source cannot change $v$ but changes the spacing of wavefronts in front of the car.

Explain the cause: in one period $T = 1/f_s$ the horn moves forward a distance $v_s T$, so each new crest is emitted closer to the last one and the observed wavelength $\lambda_o = \lambda_s - v_s T$ is shortened.
Apply $v = f_o \lambda_o$ at the man with constant $v$: a smaller $\lambda_o$ must give a larger observed frequency $f_o$ than $f_s$.
Check the distractors: the heard frequency is higher not lower, it depends on source speed not distance, and the waves do not accelerate.
Therefore the observed wavelength is less than the emitted wavelength. This is option D

A.explanation: For a source moving towards a stationary observer the heard frequency is increased, so the emitted frequency is less than the heard frequency.

B.explanation: With constant car velocity and constant source frequency the Doppler-shifted frequency is constant and does not change with separation distance.

C.explanation: Sound speed in still air is constant at about the same value, so the waves travel at constant speed and do not accelerate towards the man.

D.explanation: The approaching horn chases its own wavefronts so they are crowded together ahead of the car, giving a shorter observed wavelength.
